title: Inference Rapid Aide — Ops Cheatlist (WIP)
content:
Purpose: quick, skimmable aide for sellers and ops engineers to rescue a pilot or demo that is starting to slip because of latency/cost/quality concerns. This is intentionally terse — think pocket cheatlist that a seller can screenshot and share with an SRE or platform engineer in 2 minutes.

Audience: SEs, Sellers on pilot calls, field SREs supporting pilots, buyer-POCs (technical). Focus: 30–90 minute triage + short-term mitigations to keep a pilot live while we stabilise a long-term plan.

One-liner to customer: 'We can keep your experience within the target SLO within 24–48 hours using safe fallbacks and a short canary plan, without sacrificing measurable quality on your core flows.'

30s pitch (sellers):
- Problem: spikes in tail latency or token cost disrupting demo/pilot.
- Quick fix: route high-latency requests to a lower-cost variant + enable prefix caching for repeat prompts.
- Outcome: predictable latency and lower cost while we investigate root cause.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Confirm scope: which API routes are failing or slow (chat/generate/embeddings)? Ask for route ids and sample request payloads.
- Verify SLOs and target latency window (p95/p99 thresholds).
- Check model variant: are you on a large unquantized model (eg. non-quantized llamaX)? If yes, propose a smaller quantized variant as fallback.
- Look at recent traffic: sudden sequence-length increase or bursty cold-starts? Recommend temporary rate-limit smoothing.
- Cacheable prefixes: identify repeated system/instruction prefixes; enable prefix/KV caching on the session.
- If cost spike: turn on token limit caps for non-critical routes or reduce max_tokens by 20–40%.

Rapid fixes (apply within 1 hour):
- Routing: set per-route policy to prefer a cheaper regional cluster or model variant for non-critical traffic (example command snippet: route.setPolicy(routeId, {preferredModels: ["redwood-small-q4"]})). 
- Autoscale: temporarily raise min instances on the dedicated pool for the account to avoid cold-starts; track estimated cost impact before enabling.
- Quantization flip: switch to verified 8-bit quantized build for the active variant (note: test a single canary user first).
- Throttle non-owner tokens: apply stricter rate-limits for background/ingestion endpoints.

Deeper diagnostics (next 24–48 hours):
- Instrument: add token-level debug sampling for affected routes for 6–12 hours (low sample rate).
- Perf profiles: collect kernel selection and sequence-length distribution on serving nodes.
- Recreate: run synthetic replay of production traffic against candidate fallback to validate quality delta and latency.
- Eval: run a small, focused human eval of 50 samples on the fallback to quantify regression risk.

Objections + suggested replies (seller script):
- "We can’t afford worse quality" → "We stage the fallback to a small % and run a rapid eval; worst-case visible change is limited to 1% of requests while we stabilise."
- "This will increase cost" → "Short-term cost may rise for autoscale, but route and token caps lower per-token costs; net impact is neutralized once stable policies are in place."
- "Security/compliance concerns with model variants" → "We only route to Redwood-verified variants in the same compliance boundary; for private deployments, we only change kernel/quantization settings inside their VPC."

Suggested slide flow for a 6–8 slide rescue deck (for an on-call walkthrough):
1) Title + 1-liner + urgency statement
2) What we saw (metrics snapshot: latency, cost, top routes)
3) Immediate mitigations (3 bullets: route fallback, caps, cache)
4) Quality impact & rollback plan (canary %, eval plan)
5) 24–48h investigations + owners (SRE, ML infra, SE)
6) Longer-term remediation and timeline (model tuning, batching, quantization)
7) Cost estimate & tradeoffs
8) Next steps + commit (who does what in next 24h)

Speaker notes (short):
- Slide 2: show p95/p99 before/after, call out the specific route id(s).
- Slide 3: walk through command-and-effect for each mitigation, show one-liners sellers can paste to ops.
- Slide 4: show a minimal evaluation plan template (50 samples, blind, quality threshold).

Templates & copy snippets to paste into Slack or email:
- Quick ask to SRE: "Heads up — pilot <account> seeing p99 spikes on /chat.generate. Please enable route fallback to redwood-small-q4 and prefix caching for route-id <RID>. I'll run a 50-sample eval and revert if we see >7% degradation."
- Customer-facing status: "We applied a temporary routing and caching change to stabilise latency for your pilot. No data left your VPC, and we’ll share quality metrics within 24 hours."

Pilot canary checklist (practical):
- Choose 2–5 test users to receive fallback (1%–5% traffic).
- Start token-level sampling (tagged).
- Run blind human eval (50 samples) within 24h.
- If quality loss <= threshold (agreed upstream), expand to 25% and repeat.
- If regression > threshold, rollback immediately and re-evaluate alternative variant.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a concise automated command (CLI) to create per-route fallback policies — Sprint ticket JIRA-1985.
- Confirm whether private deployment customers accept auto-quantization toggles (legal sign-off?).
- Create a one-click Slack snippet generator in Console (UX spike).

References / helpful links: Confluence playbook, JIRA-1234 for past pilot, internal kernel-selection notes.

Next steps for this doc:
- Short-term: align with SRE on exact command snippets for routing and caching (owner: Miguel).
- Mid-term: build small Console microflow to apply these mitigations with safety checks (owner: James).
- Content: run this through one SE rehearsal and capture feedback (owner: Priya).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language buyer friendly; avoid mentioning kernel names to non-technical PO unless they ask.
- Add a 1-line metric comparator widget for the slide (p95 before / after) — ask analytics to template it.
- This lives in shared playbook; pull into the seller pocket cards after iteration 2.

End of doc.

Revision history: initial WIP 2024-11-12 by Priya. Collab edits 2024-11-26 (James) and 2024-12-01 (Ava).
